subject: Legacy rate alignment request — VP/CFO signoff needed
messages:
From: Derek Shaw <derek@bluerocktx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Legacy rate alignment for migration

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the calls last week. We’re on a tight procurement timeline — our board wants the contract signed by mid-December so we can migrate a subset of workloads in Q1. The legal team surfaced a gap: our current engagement with Redwood under the old pilot agreement had materially lower unit rates for embedding inference (legacy volume slab). Procurement is pushing to preserve that rate for the first 3 billing cycles as we transition.

Can Redwood provide a retroactive alignment to the legacy slab for invoices billed since the migration pilot started (Jul–Oct)? If not full parity, would you consider a one-time onboarding credit to make us whole through the first quarter?

We’ve attached a short procurement summary and our target schedule. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks —
Derek
Derek Shaw
Head of Platform, BlueRock Therapeutics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Legacy rate alignment for migration

Derek — thanks for the context and the timeline. I’ve looped in Jonas (VP Sales) and Rishi (Finance) to evaluate options.

Quick summary from my side:
- BlueRock is a strategic target for Q1 migration and we’d like to avoid losing momentum.
- The request is for rate parity on embedding units for Jul–Oct or a one-time onboarding credit to offset the delta.
- Procurement needs a decision by ~Dec 15 to keep the board timeline.

I’ve attached a working comparison that shows the delta between the legacy slab and our current list. Jonas/Rishi — can you review and advise what Finance would be comfortable approving versus what needs VP/CFO escalation? I can prepare a short internal memo with deal economics and margin impact.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Legacy rate alignment for migration

Team — reviewed Marissa’s comparison. We should treat BlueRock as high strategic priority but protect margin and precedent. My proposed compromise:

- Offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of eligible invoice volume for Jul–Oct (applied as a retro credit to next invoice).
- Convert the relationship to a 12-month Dedicated package (committed capacity) starting Jan 1; in exchange, lock an accelerated volume slab going forward.
- Require a committed minimum usage for the first 6 months to avoid adverse selection.

Finance: is the 10% credit within tolerances? If we can get revenue committed for 12 months, I’m willing to recommend this route to Markus/Finance for signoff. Marissa — please prepare a short memo with the economics and the anticipated ARR/TPV impact. I’ll attach a draft term sheet for the customer to review.

Attaching a draft compromise term sheet for context.

Jonas Weber
VP Sales

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Legacy rate alignment for migration

Jonas/Marissa — thanks. A few finance points:

- A one-time 10% credit is likely acceptable operationally, but we need clarity on revenue recognition. If the credit is applied retroactively it reduces billed revenue for prior periods and could impact Q4 guidance.
- Option: apply credit as a contra-invoice in Q1 (booked against Q1 revenue) and treat the net impact as a customer concession — less impact to Q4. We will need legal to sign off on amortization and AR adjustments.
- We must not set a public precedent without requiring the 12-month commitment in writing.

Marissa — please include: expected TPV for the first 12 months, estimated gross margin delta from the credit, and proposed contract language for the commitment (I can coordinate with accounting/legal on the recognition treatment). If you can get a quick signed LOI committing to the Dedicated package, that will materially reduce the risk.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Finance

Jonas/Rishi/Markus — forwarding the assembled memo and economics so we can get an official signoff for the proposed compromise. I recommend the path Jonas outlined: 10% one-time onboarding credit applied retroactively (operationally handled as a Q1 contra-invoice per Rishi’s note) in exchange for a 12-month Dedicated commitment starting Jan 1 and a minimum usage clause for months 1–6.

Attached: internal-escalation-memo.pdf (covers ARR/TPV impact, margin analysis), legacy-rate-comparison.xlsx (customer vs. list), compromise-term-sheet.pdf (customer-facing).

Key asks:
- Jonas: confirm commercial terms as final.
- Rishi: confirm accounting treatment OK to apply credit as contra-invoice in Q1 (minimizes Q4 hit).
- Markus (VP/CFO): please review the attached memo and reply to this thread with Approve / Reject / Need changes. If approved, I’ll finalize the term sheet and get a signed LOI from BlueRock by Dec 10.

Proposed approval text (so it’s auditable): "Approved: 10% onboarding credit to BlueRock (BR-2026-041) conditioned on 12-month Dedicated commitment and minimum usage; apply credit as contra-invoice in Q1 per finance guidance."

Thanks all — I’m standing by to finalize paperwork.

Marissa Cole
